The science isn't settled. The science is never settled. Also I think it's pretty obvious that not everyone agrees that the models work. There is a large user base on this site that has no interest in learning how the models work, and would rather say "blah blah blah, the news is rigged, scientists are making it all up!" without taking the time to learn how the models work, or educate themselves on why there is a scientific consensus.

On the other hand there are a bunch of people who don't bother to learn how the models work, or why there is a scientific consensus on climate change, and just parrot what they hear from IFL Science.

Then there are a small group of people who have taken the time to learn how the models work, and why there is a consensus on climate change. They understand that the science is never settled. They also understand that climate change is real (since the climate is changing) and that statistical analysis of the data can be manipulated in different ways to build more and more accurate models. This is why every few years we hear that global warming is better/worse than we thought before, and also why we have things like this current article that say climate change blindsides scientists.

If you look back to the 60s and 70s the scientific consensus was that global cooling would occur. We had models that showed it was true, but the actual data didn't fit the models, so new models were built that accounted for different variables, and the most correct ones were taken and modified further to make more and more correct models. This cycle will never stop because we can always be more correct. That isn't to say that less accurate models aren't created as well. They just don't catch on and are forgotten, because who needs broken climate models? This also means that there is always going to be an inherent inaccuracy in our predictive models.

Opponents to the climate change is real camp like to grab on to these gaps in our understanding. The problem for them is that the gaps are always shrinking. It's the same as the god of the gaps argument. Since no one can prove that god doesn't exist (it's impossible to prove a negative so far) deists cling onto the gaps in our scientific knowledge and claim that god did it, even though the gaps in our knowledge have been shrinking exponentially for the last eight thousand years.
